summary: New actual nonskeletal Radon-branch equations, off-Gauss mass<=1: full dual finite iff integral depth-tail^(3/2) finite; unbounded G solutions included. Whole Dirac remains open.
detailedSummary: Exact mixed B(qc,qd)=delta_g+delta_xmin gives finite mixtures and arbitrary Radon depths via actual uniform closure and decreasing C presentations. S=integral tail^(3/2), E=-1/3-S/3,D=1/6+2S/3; all-G uniqueness and canonical nonordered representation in this sector. Explicit unbounded example E=-4/3,D=13/6. Restricted whole-Dirac objective remains3/8 at depth1/8, not its full dual.
text:
Using earlier own n1 only at its explicitly reconstructed analytic foundation boundary, there is a new complete prescribed NONSKELETAL Radon-branch equation sector, including unbounded finite-energy weights. It is strictly larger than the previous one-depth two-atom sector and does not solve unchanged P16.7.

Let g=sigma(0), P=(1,1) in the injective chart U={|ri|<1/4}, wi=zi-1, and x_c the joint bidisc Gauss point |wi|<=exp(-c), c>0. Put x_0=g. Keep q0=sum xi(1-xi)/2-1/4, xi=ri-floor ri. Define gamma=max(0,-log max(|w1|,|w2|)) on U and zero outside, with gamma(P)=infinity. This is actual extended continuous, finite off P, and gamma(x_c)=c. For each c, vc=log max(exp(-c),|w1|,|w2|,|w1w2|)-log(A1A2)=-min(c,gamma), Ai=max(1,|zi|)=max(1,|wi|), and qc=q0+vc. If either |wi|>=1 the correction is zero; if either |zi| differs from1 the same is true. Hence there is genuine ordinary collar gluing on1/8<max|ri|<1/4. Deck units2,3 cause no descent assertion because the translated coordinates are used only on this injective chart. The positive constant slot permits omission of vanishing polynomial slots; local smooth convex maxima of unit logarithms plus actual smooth harmonic terms give qc in the entire original C.

The decisive NEW actual mixed product is B(qc,qd)=delta_g+delta_xmin(c,d). Here is its proof, beyond the earlier square and baseline products MA(q0)=2delta_g, MA(qc)=delta_g+delta_xc, B(q0,qc)=2delta_g, which are reconstructed by the exact fixed-coordinate/translation/inversion fibre formulas in n1. Suppose c<d and both wi are nonzero. Write bi=log|wi|, m=max(b1,b2). If some bi>=0 the two potentials agree locally with max(b1,b2,b1+b2), whose square is supported only at the inverse-coordinate unit Gauss g with coefficient1. In the negative quadrant, for m<-c the c-potential is constant; for m>-c both are locally max(b1,b2), a one-ratio potential with zero square. At m=-c and b1!=b2 the d-potential is one unit logarithm, hence has zero Hessian. At b1=b2=-c, DD Ld=DD log max(1,|w1/w2|) is the fixed ratio Gauss curve current by the d1 formula. On that curve over H(eta1), Lc restricts to log max(exp(-c),|w2|). Fixed-current restriction and the curve d1 formula yield the singleton x_c, coefficient1. The primitive exponent bijection(i,j)->(i,i+j) identifies this iterated Gauss norm with the original joint Gauss norm. Polynomial zeros permit slot removal and one-coordinate vanishing. Outside U the baseline top measure is zero. This covers every actual analytic point and identifies the Radon product on every continuous analytic test, not just its projection.

For finite prescribed depths0<c1<...<cN and massesmk>0, M=sum mk<=1, set alphak=sqrt(sum_(j>=k)mj), alpha_(N+1)=0, betak=alphak-alpha_(k+1). The actual convex combination q=q0+sum betak vc_k has sum beta=sqrt M<=1. Multilinearity gives at x_ck the coefficient beta_k²+2beta_k sum_(j>k)betaj=alpha_k²-alpha_(k+1)²=mk. The Gauss coefficient is2-M. Thus MA(q)=(2-M)delta_g+sum mk delta_xck, exactly the input. It has sup0 and range[-1/4-sum beta_k ck,0]. Write d(c)=sum beta_k min(c,ck), S=sum mk d(ck). Along q0+h(q-q0), MA=(2-h²M)delta_g+h²sum mk delta_xck; the direction has value0 at g and -d(ck) at each xck. Actual first variation gives E'= -h²S. Hence E(q)=-1/3-S/3 and its target moment is-1/2-S. Entire-C tangent concavity gives attained FULL D=1/6+2S/3. An actual decreasing presentation is q+2^-n.

Now let zeta be ANY finite positive Radon depth measure on(0,infinity) with M=zeta((0,infinity))<=1. Put T(t)=zeta((t,infinity)), alpha(t)=sqrt(T(t)), d_C(c)=int_0^min(c,C) alpha(t)dt, S_C=int_0^C T(t)^1.5dt, S=lim S_C. The actual raw-mass-two target is mu_zeta=(2-M)delta_g+pushforward_(c->x_c) zeta. There is no mass at infinite depth P. This pushforward is Radon by continuous pushforward on compact depth intervals and total-variation approximation by their restrictions.

THEOREM: FULL D(mu_zeta) is finite if and only if S<infinity. In that case q_zeta=q0-d(gamma), d(c)=int_0^c sqrt(T(t))dt, has an ACTUAL original-C continuous decreasing presentation q_n=q0-d_n(gamma), finite lower energy, and genuine original-G operator MA(q_zeta)=mu_zeta. Its energy is-1/3-S/3, target moment-1/2-S, and FULL D=1/6+2S/3. It is unique modulo constants among ALL actual original G solutions. It is bounded continuous exactly when int_0^infinity sqrt(T(t))dt<infinity; otherwise it is extended continuous, finite and locally continuous off P, and -infinity at P.

Construction and proof of the criterion: at finite C push zeta to depths min(c,C), retaining its mass. Approximate this measure by finite partition masses placed at positive right endpoints. Tails converge at every non-atomic threshold, hence almost everywhere; dominated convergence gives L1 convergence of square-root tails on[0,C]. The finite solutions converge uniformly, with error at most this L1 error, to the actual q_C. Entire minimal-sheaf closure proves q_C in C with the same ordinary collar. Independently, actual recursive-product continuity and continuous c->x_c give MA(q_C)=(2-M)delta_g+pushforward_(c->x_min(c,C))zeta against every continuous analytic test. Tonelli gives int d_C(c) zeta(dc)=int_0^C sqrt(T(t))zeta([t,infinity))dt=S_C; atomic endpoints affect no Lebesgue integral. Uniform product/energy continuity, or actual first variation, gives E(q_C)=-1/3-S_C/3 and int q_C MA(q_C)=-1/2-S_C. Also int q_C mu_zeta=-1/2-S_C.

The q_n are continuous, normalized, nonpositive and genuinely decreasing on all X. If S is finite they have finite lower energy, which supplies the required actual G presentation. Their genuine bounded MA measures converge to mu_zeta: a continuous test h has discrepancy at most2||h|| zeta((n,infinity)). The canonical generated operator is this weak limit. Tonelli as n tends to infinity gives the finite target moment. For every fixed a in the ENTIRE C, tangent at q_n and weak convergence give E(a)-int a mu_zeta<=1/6+2S/3. The bounded competitors q_n give equality in the supremum since their objectives tend to that value. If S is infinite those same actual bounded competitors force FULL D=infinity; no positivity/operator is assigned to an ineligible Borel function. Boundedness and extended continuity follow from the continuous extended gamma and monotone d; uniform convergence occurs if d(infinity)<infinity.

Nonordered representation: q_n maximizes the original full dual with exact deficit2(S-S_n)/3. n1 coercivity bounds energies of q_n and every late normalized maximizing family. Its midpoint inequality I(a_i,q_n)<=4(epsilon_i+2(S-S_n)/3), followed by the energy/fixed-test/full-point/weak-test moduli, identifies canonical energy, full-point values and genuine weak MA with the already constructed q_zeta and mu_zeta. Full points differ from rigid P and q_n there is eventually q_zeta. Passing the uniform third-slot estimate against the energy-bounded MA(q_n) to mu_zeta gives int|a_i-a_j|mu_zeta<=T_L(I(a_i,a_j)); completeness and product-index comparison yield canonical L1(mu_zeta) convergence to q_zeta. The all-affinoid finite Shilov formula identifies the ordinary upper relaxation with the already constructed continuous q_zeta off P; at P it does so by continuity if finite, and by arbitrarily negative bounds on ordinary neighborhoods if infinite. Every fast limit agrees with q_zeta at g and each x_c, giving J=K=0. Other raw Borel points receive no declared positivity or MA.

Uniqueness retains actual generated antecedents. For any b_n decreasing to v with finite lower energy, compact strict comparison between two presentations plus epsilon constants proves limiting energy canonicity. Apply it to finite convex combinations and interpolate their cubic energy polynomials at a finite unisolvent set. First variations of E((1-t)b_n+tw) and E(tb_n) give a canonical weak MA against the dense span of C, then all continuous tests. If e=lim E(b_n), p=lim int b_n MA(b_n), passing tangent gives D(lambda)<=e-p; monotone convergence of the full dual bound makes v lambda-integrable. The ordered cubic cocycle gives0<=int(b_n-b_l)MA(b_l)<=3(Eb_n-Eb_l), l>=n. Pass l against fixed b_n, then n by integrability to get p=int v lambda and D(lambda)=e-int v lambda. Thus the normalized presentation maximizes. Its suprema decrease to finite sup v by compact nested superlevel sets and E(b_n)<=2sup b_n. If lambda=mu_zeta, the proved full-point limits give v-s=q_zeta densely. USC of the already generated v-s and continuity of q_zeta exclude smaller values off P. Finite Shilov maxima of actual continuous presentation potentials, followed by shrinking neighborhoods, exclude larger values. At P continuity handles the finite case; arbitrarily negative neighboring full-point values force v(P)=-infinity in the remaining case. This proves equality at EVERY actual point, hence uniqueness modulo constants.

Concrete NEW unbounded example: zeta=c^-2 dc on[1,infinity), mass1. Its tail is1 below1 and t^-1 above1, so S=3 but int sqrt(T)=infinity. The target delta_g+int_1^infinity delta_xc c^-2dc has actual generated solution with correction-gamma up to depth1 and -(2sqrt(gamma)-1) thereafter, value-infinity only at P. E=-4/3, FULL D=13/6; the actual q_n have E=-4/3+2/(3sqrt n). A genuinely two-depth bounded example is delta_g+(3/4)delta_x1/8+(1/4)delta_x1/4, with S=9/64,E=-73/192,D=25/96.

For the priority whole target2delta_xa, this entire branch family has restricted objective supremum exactly1/6+5a/3, attained by zeta=delta_a. Indeed its objective is1/6+int_0^a(2alpha-alpha³/3)dt-int_a^infinity alpha³/3 dt, with0<=alpha<=1. The first integrand is strictly increasing and at most5/3; the second contribution is nonpositive. Every cutoff obeys the same bound. For a=1/8 the restricted supremum is3/8, so this enlarged branch route does not improve the previous whole-Dirac competitor. This is NOT an upper bound on the ORIGINAL FULL dual, nor nonexistence outside this family.
